reference: If she stays still, the dragonfly will stay on the reed.
sk: Ak vydrží nehybne, vážka zostane na trstine.
cz: Když vydrží nehybně, vážka zůstane na rákosu.
acceptable: If {she|he} {stays still|keeps still|remains still|stays motionless|remains motionless|doesn't move}, the dragonfly will {stay|remain} on the reed.
The dragonfly will {stay|remain} on the reed if {she|he} {stays still|keeps still|remains still|stays motionless|doesn't move}.

mistakes.text: If {she|he} will stay still, the dragonfly will stay on the reed.
mistakes.feedback_sk: Po „if“ patrí v First Conditional Present Simple: „if she stays“, nie „will stay“.
mistakes.feedback_cz: Po „if“ patří ve First Conditional Present Simple: „if she stays“, ne „will stay“.
mistakes.feedback_en: In First Conditional use Present Simple after “if”: “if she stays”, not “will stay”.

mistakes.text: If {she|he} stay still, the dragonfly will stay on the reed.
If {she|he} stays still, the dragonfly stays on the reed.
mistakes.feedback_sk: Ide o konkrétny budúci následok, preto v First Conditional patrí „will stay“.
mistakes.feedback_cz: Jde o konkrétní budoucí následek, proto ve First Conditional patří „will stay“.
mistakes.feedback_en: This is one specific future result, so First Conditional uses “will stay”.

mistakes.text: If {she|he} stays quiet, the dragonfly will stay on the reed.
mistakes.feedback_en: Not moving is “still”; “quiet” means making no sound.

mistakes.text: If {she|he} stays still, the dragonfly will stay in the reed.
mistakes.feedback_sk: Vážka sedí na jednom steble, preto „on the reed“, nie „in the reed“.
mistakes.feedback_cz: Vážka sedí na jednom stéble, proto „on the reed“, ne „in the reed“.
mistakes.feedback_en: The dragonfly sits on top of one reed, so use “on the reed”, not “in”.

source_issues: Slovak and Czech drop the subject pronoun, so “she” is not given; “he” is accepted too.
